{{Short description|Mathematics writer and lecturer}}
'''Charles Wilderman Trigg''' (February 7, 1898, Baltimore, Maryland – June 28, 1989, San Diego, California)<ref name=obit>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-charles-w-trigg-o/8462987/ obituary] [[Los Angeles Times]], July 9, 1989</ref> was a mathematics writer and lecturer for many years at the [[University of Southern California]].  He was considered one of the foremost recreational mathematicians of the twentieth century and was the book review editor of the ''[[Journal of Recreational Mathematics]]''.<ref name=calgary>[https://libguides.ucalgary.ca/c.php?g=255446&p=1703613 Library Archives and Special Collections: Recreational Mathematics] [[University of Calgary]]</ref><ref>[https://albertaonrecord.ca/trigg-charles-w-1898-1989 Trigg, Charles W., 1898-1989] Archives, Society of Alberta</ref>

==Education and career==
Trigg got a B.S. in chemical engineering at  [[Baltimore Polytechnic Institute]] in 1914, another B.S. in chemical engineering at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in 1917, and an M.A. at the [[University of Southern California]] in 1931.<ref name=archives>[https://sova.si.edu/record/NMAH.AC.0411 Guide to the Charles W. Trigg Papers] Archives Center, Smithsonian Institution, [[National Museum of American History]], 2023</ref>

Until 1950 his main field of research was the production of coffee, first at the [[Mellon Institute of Industrial Research|Mellon Institute]] in Pittsburgh (1916-1920), and then at [[Trung Nguyên|King Coffee Products]] in Detroit.  He was granted five patents related to coffee processing.<ref name=archives/>

In 1950 he became a lecturer at the University of Southern California, where he stayed until 1966.  In 1967 he wrote his very popular book, ''Mathematical Quickies: 270 Stimulating Problems with Solutions''.<ref name=google>[https://books.google.com/books?id=9W6GQ42BRR0C ''Mathematical Quickies: 270 Stimulating Problems with Solutions'' Review] by [[Google Books]]</ref><ref>[https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/6-1/review2.pdf Review of ''Mathematical Quickies'' by Charles W. Trigg] Howard Eves, University of Maine</ref> A reviewer said, "For the mathematics enthusiast of any age or level of sophisitcation, this stimulating treasury of unusual math problems offers unlimited opportunity for mind-biggling recreation."<ref name=google/>

==Publications==
* 1973: "Palindromic Triangular Numbers" (with Raphael Robinson), [[Journal of Recreational Mathematics|J. Recr. Math]]. Vol. 6, pp.&nbsp;146–147
* 1967: ''Mathematical Quickies: 270 Stimulating Problems with Solutions'', McGraw Hill, 1967, {{ISBN|0486249492}}
* 1934: "[https://www.jstor.org/stable/2301005 E69]" [[The American Mathematical Monthly|Amer. Math. Monthly]], Vol. 41, No. 5, May, 1934, p.&nbsp;332
